result.topic_en: This is the title page and opening of Euler's paper on a new method for the calculus of variations. It explains that any expression built from x and y, with y a function of x, can be treated as a function of x alone. It then begins sorting such expressions into three kinds.

Auctore

1.
Si detur aequatio quaecunque inter binas variabiles
$x$ et $y$ ſeu quod eodem redit, ſi $y$ fuerit fun-
ctio quaecunque ipſius $x$, tum omnes expreſſiones
quomodocunque ex his duabus quantitatibus $x$ et $y$
formatae et compoſitae tamquam functiones vnius
variabilis $x$, ſpectari poterunt, ita vt pro quouis
valore determinato ipſius $x$, determinatos quoque
valores ſortiantur.
2. Huiusmodi autem expreſſionum ex quanti-
tatibus $x$ et $y$ formatarum, tria genera conſtitui
conuenit; ad quorum primum referimus omnes il-

et $y$ occurrunt et per operationes quaſcunque ſiue
algebraicas ſiue etiam tranſcendentes inter ſe ſunt
complicatae, cuiusmodi ſunt $\alpha x^{3}+\beta xy+\gamma y^{3}$,

items.english: Now it is convenient to establish three kinds of such expressions formed from the quantities x and y.

items.quote:
tum omnes expreſſiones
quomodocunque ex his duabus quantitatibus $x$ et $y$
formatae et compoſitae tamquam functiones vnius
variabilis $x$, ſpectari poterunt
items.english: Then all expressions formed and composed in any way from these two quantities x and y can be regarded as functions of the single variable x.
